name: Endless Loop Round Sling
title: Endless Loop Round Sling for Crane and Rigging Work
meta: An endless loop round sling for crane picks and heavy rigging on tree removals. How to choke or basket it, read the tag, and inspect it before every lift.
tagline: A soft, endless round sling for crane picks and heavy rigging points.
summary: An endless loop round sling is a continuous polyester sling with no eyes, so you can choke, basket, or hitch it straight around a stem. Crews use it for crane picks, heavy rigging points, and anywhere a soft sling is kinder to the bark than chain.
highlights: Endless loop, no eyes to wear out
Soft on bark and on hardware
Works in choker, basket, or vertical hitch
Color and tag show the rated capacity
Light to carry up the tree or hang on the boom
specs: Load-bearing core yarns inside a protective cover
Printed on the sling tag; varies by size

body.h: Where a round sling fits on a tree job
p: On a crane removal the round sling is usually the first thing on the pick. Choke it around the stem above the cut, set the hook, and let the operator take the weight before the saw goes in. Because it has no eyes and no hardware, it wraps tight to the wood, lies flat, and is easy to free once the piece is on the ground.

Round slings also earn their keep as heavy rigging points for a block, and as basket slings for lifting logs at the landing. Compared with wire rope or chain they are lighter, quieter, and far less likely to scar the trunk you are leaving behind. See the rest of our crane slings for other lengths and capacities.

Every round sling carries a tag with its rated capacity for each hitch. A choker hitch rates lower than a vertical pull, and a basket depends on the angle of the legs, so read the tag for the way you are actually rigging it. If the tag is missing or unreadable, the sling is out of service.

The cover protects the core but it is not cut-proof. Keep the sling away from the saw, pad sharp edges, and never tie knots in it. Before each lift, look for cuts, burns, melted or stiff spots, exposed core yarns, and broken stitching. Crane work around trees should follow ANSI Z133, the sling maker's instructions, and a qualified operator and rigger.

faq.q: Can I choke an endless round sling around a stem?
faq.a: Yes. Choking is one of the most common ways to use it on a crane pick. Use the choker rating on the tag, which is lower than the vertical rating.

faq.q: How long does a round sling last?
faq.a: It depends on use and care. Retire it as soon as you find cuts, heat damage, exposed core yarns, or a missing tag.

name: Husqvarna 530iPT Battery Pole Saw (Tool Only)
title: Husqvarna 530iPT Battery Pole Saw, Tool Only
h1: Husqvarna 530iPT Battery Pole Saw (No Battery or Charger)
meta: The Husqvarna 530iPT telescoping battery pole saw, sold as a bare tool for crews already on Husqvarna 36V batteries. What it cuts, reach, and buying tips.
tagline: A telescoping 36V pole saw for ground pruning, sold without battery or charger.
summary: The Husqvarna 530iPT is a telescoping battery pole saw built for pruning and clearance work from the ground. This listing is the bare tool, aimed at crews that already run Husqvarna 36V batteries and chargers.
highlights: Quiet, no fuel mix, no exhaust
Good fit for lift clearance and street pruning
Bare tool: battery and charger sold separately
specs: Pole saw only; no battery or charger

p: A battery pole saw shines on the jobs where a gas pole saw is overkill: raising canopies over sidewalks, clearing limbs off a roof line, and cleaning up after a climber without sending anyone back up. With no pull cord and no exhaust it starts on the trigger, runs quiet enough for residential streets, and does not stink up a client's patio.

The telescoping shaft lets one tool cover low limbs and high ones. Keep cuts within the bar's capacity, undercut heavier limbs to stop bark tearing, and stand out from under the drop zone. Browse other battery-powered equipment if you are building out a cordless kit.

Buying tool-only makes sense if you already own Husqvarna 36V batteries from a top-handle saw, blower, or trimmer. If you are new to the platform, price a battery and charger alongside it, since runtime depends on the battery you pair with it.

Wear a helmet, eye protection, and gloves, keep the saw well clear of power lines, and only let trained workers operate it near energized conductors. Follow ANSI Z133 and the Husqvarna operator's manual for chain tension, lubrication, and maintenance.

faq.q: Does the 530iPT come with a battery?
faq.a: Not this version. It is sold as a bare tool, so you need a compatible Husqvarna 36V battery and charger.

faq.q: Can I use a pole saw near power lines?
faq.a: Only qualified line-clearance workers should work near energized lines. Everyone else must keep the required clearance distances under ANSI Z133.

name: Husqvarna Fixed Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
title: Husqvarna Fixed Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
h1: Husqvarna Fixed Pulley Pruner with Adapter and Rope
meta: A Husqvarna fixed pulley pruner head with adapter and pull rope for clean pole cuts on small limbs. Where it fits in a pole kit and how to keep it cutting.
tagline: A rope-pull bypass pruner head that mounts on a pole for clean cuts out of reach.
summary: This Husqvarna pulley pruner is a rope-operated pruner head that mounts to a pole with the included adapter. It makes clean, flush cuts on small limbs and suckers that are out of reach, without a saw.
highlights: Fixed pulley head for added cutting force
Pairs with a pole saw head on the same pole set
specs: Pole adapter (check fit with your pole system)

body.h: What a pulley pruner is good for
p: A pole pruner does the small, fussy cuts a pole saw does poorly: water sprouts, suckers, deadwood twigs, and fine thinning cuts where you want a clean collar cut instead of a ragged saw kerf. The pulley in the head multiplies your pull on the rope, so the blade closes with more force than a straight lever would give you.

Most crews carry a pruner head and a saw head for the same pole set and swap between them as the job changes. Check that the adapter matches your poles before you head out. You can find poles and complete setups in our poles and kits section.

Keep the blade sharp and the pivot clean and lightly oiled; a dull pruner crushes bark instead of cutting it. Check the pull rope for wear where it runs through the pulley and replace it before it frays through. Do not force the head on wood larger than it is built to cut, since that bends the blade and opens up the bypass gap.
Wear eye protection and a helmet when cutting overhead. Never use a pole tool near energized power lines unless you are a qualified line-clearance worker following ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Does the pruner fit any pole?
faq.a: It mounts with the included adapter. Confirm the adapter matches your pole system before buying.

faq.q: How big a limb can it cut?
faq.a: Pole pruners are meant for small limbs. Use a pole saw for anything thick enough that the pruner strains to close.

name: Husqvarna Pole Saw Head with Center Saw Blade Mount
title: Husqvarna Pole Saw Head with Center Blade Mount
h1: Husqvarna Pole Saw Head with Center Saw Blade Mount
meta: A Husqvarna pole saw head with a center blade mount, so the blade lines up with the pole for straight pulls. How it fits a pole kit and what to check first.
tagline: A pole saw head that centers the blade on the pole for straighter cuts.
summary: This Husqvarna pole saw head holds a pruning saw blade on a center mount, so the blade runs in line with the pole. That alignment makes pull strokes straighter and keeps the saw from twisting in the cut.
highlights: Center blade mount keeps the blade in line with the pole
Fits a pole saw blade for overhead cutting
Pairs with a pruner head on the same pole set

p: When the blade sits off to one side of the pole, every pull stroke tries to roll the saw over, and the cut wanders. A center mount puts the blade right on the pole's axis, so your pull goes straight into the kerf. On long reaches that difference is easy to feel in your shoulders by the end of the day.
The head lets you swap blades as they wear and move between a saw and a pruner head on one set of poles. See the full range of pole saws and scabbards for blades and covers.

Make sure the head and blade match your pole system and that the blade bolts are snug before every use; a loose blade chatters and can drop out of the cut. Clean sap off the blade and head at the end of the day and store the saw in a scabbard to protect the teeth and the crew.

Cut from the side, not from directly under the limb, and keep a clear drop zone. Wear a helmet and eye protection, and stay clear of power lines unless you are qualified for line clearance under ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Does this include a saw blade?
faq.a: It is listed as a saw head. Check the listing for whether a blade is included, and match any blade to the mount.

faq.q: Will it fit my poles?
faq.a: It is designed for Husqvarna pole systems. Confirm the fitting before buying for another brand of pole.

name: ISC Offset Oval Quadlock Carabiner with Captive Pin
title: ISC Offset Oval Quadlock Carabiner with Captive Pin
h1: ISC Offset Oval Quadlock Carabiner with Captive Pin
meta: The ISC offset oval quadlock carabiner with a captive pin that keeps it oriented on a device or bridge. Gate action, uses on the saddle, and inspection tips.
tagline: A four-action auto-locking offset oval with a captive pin to hold it in place.
summary: The ISC offset oval quadlock carabiner pairs a four-stage auto-locking gate with a captive pin that keeps the carabiner from rotating out of position. Climbers use it where a connector should stay put, such as on a device, pulley, or bridge.
highlights: Quadlock gate: four separate actions to open
Captive pin holds the carabiner in position
Good for connections that should not rotate or cross-load

body.h: What the captive pin and quadlock gate do
p: A loose carabiner can rotate until it loads across the gate, which is exactly how connectors fail. The captive pin closes off part of the carabiner so whatever is clipped in, such as a pulley, device, or eye, stays in the right spot and the carabiner loads along its spine.

The quadlock gate takes four deliberate actions to open. That is more fiddly with gloves than a triple lock, but it is much harder for a branch, rope, or bridge to roll it open by accident. Compare it with other auto-locking carabiners if you prefer a quicker gate.

Load the carabiner only along its major axis and check the gate closes and locks fully every time you clip it. Do not let it rest across an edge or a limb, and do not three-way load it unless the maker allows it.

Inspect before each climb for sharp edges, grooves, cracks, and a sticky or slow gate, and retire any carabiner that has been dropped onto a hard surface from height. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: What does quadlock mean?
faq.a: The gate needs four separate actions to open. It is slower to operate than a triple lock but more resistant to accidental opening.

faq.q: Can I remove the captive pin?
faq.a: Follow ISC's instructions. Do not modify a life-support connector beyond what the manufacturer allows.

name: Kask Zenith X2 Hi-Viz Climbing Helmet
title: Kask Zenith X2 Hi-Viz Climbing Helmet
h1: Kask Zenith X2 Hi-Viz Climbing Helmet
meta: The Kask Zenith X2 in hi-viz: a climbing-style work helmet for tree crews who want to be seen. Fit, accessories, and what to check on the label before buying.
tagline: A hi-viz climbing-style work helmet for arborists working near traffic and machines.
summary: The Kask Zenith X2 is a climbing-style work helmet with a chinstrap, and the hi-viz shell makes you easy to spot from the ground, the road, or the chipper. It suits climbers and ground crew who wear a helmet all day.
highlights: Rear dial adjustment for a snug fit
Accepts Kask visors and ear muffs (check fit)

body.h: Why tree crews pick the Zenith X2
p: A climbing-style helmet stays on when you are upside down in a canopy or bent over a stump, which an old cap-style hard hat with no chinstrap will not. The Zenith X2 adds a hi-viz shell, a real advantage on roadside jobs, in storm cleanup, and anywhere a groundie or machine operator needs to see where you are.
Most crews outfit it with a mesh visor and helmet-mounted ear muffs so face and hearing protection are always on. Compare other climbing helmets if you want a vented or lighter shell.

Set the headband so the helmet sits level and does not move when you shake your head, then snug the chinstrap. Check the label for the standards the helmet is certified to and make sure they match what your employer and ANSI Z133 require for the work you do.

Inspect the shell and harness before each day, and replace the helmet after any significant impact or when the maker's service life is up. Clean it with mild soap and water only; solvents and stickers with strong adhesives can weaken the shell.

faq.q: Can I add a visor and ear muffs?
faq.a: Yes. Kask makes visors and ear muff adapters for its helmets. Confirm the accessory is listed as compatible with the Zenith X2.

faq.q: Is the Zenith X2 good for ground crew too?
faq.a: Yes. The hi-viz shell and chinstrap make it a good all-day helmet for ground work as well as climbing.

name: Notch Sentei Replacement Blade
title: Notch Sentei Replacement Saw Blade
meta: A replacement blade for the Notch Sentei saw. Swap a dull or kinked blade instead of buying a whole new saw, and keep pruning cuts clean. Fit and care tips here.
tagline: A fresh blade for your Notch Sentei saw when the old one is dull or bent.
summary: This Notch Sentei replacement blade lets you put a new blade on your existing Sentei saw instead of replacing the whole tool. Hardened pull-stroke teeth are hard to resharpen, so a new blade is the quickest way back to clean cuts.
highlights: Direct replacement for the Notch Sentei saw
Brings back fast, clean pull-stroke cuts
Cheaper than a whole new saw

p: A pruning saw blade is a wear part. Once the teeth are rounded, the saw starts to bind, burn, and tear bark, and you work twice as hard for a ragged cut. A kinked blade is worse: it wanders in the kerf and can snap. Either way, a new blade costs a fraction of a new saw and puts the edge back in a few minutes.
Match the blade to your saw model; blades from different saws are not interchangeable even when they look similar. You can find other blades in our replacement blades section.
Tighten the blade bolt firmly so the blade does not rock in the handle, and check it again after the first few cuts. Keep fingers clear of the teeth while swapping; wear gloves.

Wipe sap off the blade at the end of the day and give it a light coat of oil to slow rust. Cut on the pull stroke and let the teeth do the work; forcing the saw on the push is what kinks blades. Keep the saw in a scabbard on the saddle and in the truck.

faq.q: Will this blade fit other Notch saws?
faq.a: It is made for the Sentei. Check the listing before fitting it to any other saw.

faq.q: Can I sharpen the old blade instead?
faq.a: Hardened pruning saw teeth are difficult to file. Replacing the blade is usually faster and gives a better result.

name: Pferd Guide Bar Dresser
title: Pferd Guide Bar Dresser for Chainsaw Bar Rails
meta: The Pferd guide bar dresser files chainsaw bar rails flat and square so the chain runs straight. When to use it, how it works, and how to keep the file sharp.
tagline: A file holder that squares up worn chainsaw bar rails so cuts run straight.
summary: The Pferd guide bar dresser holds a flat file square to the bar so you can dress worn, uneven, or burred rails. Squared-up rails keep the chain upright in the groove and stop the saw from pulling to one side.
highlights: Files bar rails flat and square
Removes burrs that rub on the chain
Helps fix a saw that cuts crooked
Small enough for the truck kit

p: Bar rails wear unevenly, especially if the chain was filed lopsided or run dull. When one rail is lower than the other the chain leans, the cut curves, and the saw fights you in every bucking cut. Rails also roll over at the edges into burrs that grab the drive links.

A bar dresser holds the file square to the side of the bar so both rails come out flat and level. Run it along the rails with steady, even strokes until the burr is gone and the rails match. You can find files and tools in our wrenches and files section.

Dress the bar when you change chains or whenever you feel a burr along the rail edge. Flip the bar each time you sharpen so it wears evenly, and clean the groove and oil holes so the chain gets oil. If the rails are badly worn, pinched, or the groove is too shallow, replace the bar instead of filing it further.
Wear gloves when handling the chain and bar, and keep the saw off with the chain brake on when you work on it. When the file stops cutting cleanly, swap in a replacement file.

faq.q: How often should I dress my bar?
faq.a: Check the rails at every chain change. Dress them whenever you feel a burr or notice the saw cutting crooked.

faq.q: Can I replace the file?
faq.a: Yes. The file is a wear part and replacement files are available.

name: Yale Phantom Replacement Friction Saver Lanyard
title: Phantom Replacement Friction Saver Lanyard
meta: A replacement Phantom rope lanyard for an adjustable friction saver. Swap a worn or glazed rope section and keep using your rings and hardware. Fit and care tips.
tagline: A fresh rope section for your Phantom adjustable friction saver.
summary: This Phantom replacement friction saver lanyard is the rope section of an adjustable friction saver, sold on its own. When the rope is worn or glazed, you can replace it and keep the rings and hardware that are still in good shape.
highlights: Replacement rope for an adjustable friction saver
Cheaper than a complete new friction saver

p: On an adjustable friction saver the rope takes the wear: it rubs on bark, gets packed with sap and grit, and glazes from heat. The rings and adjuster usually outlast it by a long way. Swapping the rope section gets the saver back in service without paying for hardware you already own.
Make sure the replacement matches your saver's design and the hardware it was built around. If in doubt, compare it with the complete friction savers we carry.

Assemble it exactly as the manufacturer's instructions show, and test it on the ground with your full weight before climbing on it. Check every connection and make sure the adjuster grips the rope securely.

Inspect the rope before each climb for cuts, glazing, flat or stiff spots, and core damage, and check the rings for grooves. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Does this include rings or the adjuster?
faq.a: It is the rope lanyard only, unless the listing says otherwise. Reuse hardware only if it passes inspection.

faq.q: Will it fit another brand of friction saver?
faq.a: It is made for the Phantom adjustable friction saver. Do not mix it with other systems unless the maker approves it.

name: Sterling TriTech Lanyard with Double Locking Snap
title: Sterling TriTech Lanyard with Double Locking Snap
h1: Sterling TriTech Lanyard with Double Locking Snap
meta: The Sterling TriTech lanyard with a double locking snap, a tough rope flipline for work positioning on spars and removals. Uses, adjusters, and inspection tips.
tagline: A tough rope flipline with a locking snap for spar work and positioning.
summary: The Sterling TriTech lanyard is a rope flipline built from Sterling's TriTech rope and finished with a double locking snap. It is a work-positioning lanyard for spurring up spars, holding position on removals, and adding a second point of attachment while cutting.
highlights: Double locking snap on the end
For work positioning and spar climbing
Pairs with a rope grab or hitch adjuster
Must be used with a chainsaw-aware cutting technique

p: A flipline wraps the stem and clips back to your saddle so you can lean back and work with both hands. On a removal it is your main point of attachment while you spur up and cut; in a spreading canopy it is a second tie-in when you cut near your climbing line. An adjuster, either a rope grab or a friction hitch, lets you shorten and lengthen it as the stem changes size.
Rope lanyards are lighter and easier on the hands than wire-core ones. See the rest of our rope lanyards to compare lengths and setups.

body.h: Cutting safely on a rope lanyard
p: A rope lanyard can be cut by a chainsaw, so keep the bar away from it, position yourself so the saw cannot drift toward it, and have a second attachment when you are cutting above or near it. Never cut while relying on a lanyard you cannot see.

Check the rope, eyes, and snap before every climb: look for cuts, glazing, fuzzing at the eye, and a snap that does not close and lock on its own. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Does it come with an adjuster?
faq.a: This listing is the lanyard with a double locking snap. Check whether an adjuster is included; many climbers add a rope grab or hitch.

faq.q: Is a rope lanyard cut-proof?
faq.a: No. Any rope lanyard can be cut by a chainsaw. Use a second attachment and keep the saw clear of it.

name: The Splice Shop Aluminum Ring
title: The Splice Shop Aluminum Ring for Climbing Systems
meta: The Splice Shop aluminum ring for friction savers, ring-and-ring setups, and custom climbing systems. How climbers use it, what to check, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A smooth aluminum ring for friction savers and custom climbing setups.
summary: The Splice Shop aluminum ring is a solid ring climbers use to build friction savers, redirects, and spliced eye-and-ring setups. Aluminum keeps it light on the saddle while giving the rope a smooth, rounded surface to run over.
highlights: Smooth radius for rope to run over
Use in friction savers and redirects
Pairs with spliced slings and eye-and-eyes
Ratings marked or listed by the maker

p: Rings are the building blocks of a lot of climbing systems. Two rings on a sling make a ring-and-ring friction saver; a single ring on a cambium saver or anchor sling makes a smooth redirect; and a ring spliced into an eye-and-eye gives a hitch or device a clean bearing point.

Aluminum rings are lighter than steel and run rope smoothly, but they wear faster when a moving rope runs over them all day. For a high-wear tie-in point, some climbers choose steel instead. Compare other climbing rings if you are deciding.

Look at the inside radius before every climb. Moving rope cuts grooves into aluminum over time, and a sharp-edged groove will damage rope. Retire the ring if you find grooves, cracks, sharp edges, or deformation, or if it has been dropped onto a hard surface from height.

Check that the ring's rating suits the system you are building and that every connection loads it the way the maker intends. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Aluminum or steel ring?
faq.a: Aluminum is lighter; steel resists wear better where rope runs over it constantly. Choose based on where it sits in your system.

faq.q: When do I retire an aluminum ring?
faq.a: When you find grooves, sharp edges, cracks, or deformation, or after it has been dropped from height onto a hard surface.

name: The Splice Shop Thimble Loop Rigging Sling 1/2 x 35 in with 14mm Ring
title: Thimble Loop Rigging Sling 1/2 x 35 in, 14mm Ring
h1: The Splice Shop Thimble Loop Rigging Sling, 1/2 x 35 in with 14mm Ring
meta: The Splice Shop thimble loop rigging sling in 1/2 x 35 in with a 14mm ring, for choking spars and setting rigging points. How it rigs, sizing, and inspection.
tagline: A 1/2 in rope ring sling with a thimble eye for spar and natural-crotch rigging.
summary: This thimble loop rigging sling from The Splice Shop uses 1/2 in rope, a 35 in length, and a 14mm ring, so you can choke a stem and build a quick rigging point. The thimble protects the loop where it meets hardware.
highlights: Use as a rigging point or a choker on the piece

p: Wrap the stem, pass the thimble loop through the ring, and cinch it down: the sling chokes tight and holds its position on a vertical spar better than a basket hitch. The ring or thimble then becomes the anchor for a block, a lowering line, or a redirect.

The thimble keeps the eye round and protects the rope where it bears on a carabiner or shackle. A 35 in sling suits small to medium stems; it will not wrap a big trunk. Look through our other heavy-duty slings for longer and heavier options.

Size the sling to the wood you are taking down and to the rest of the system, including the rope, block, and anchor. A 1/2 in sling is meant for pruning-size wood and small tops, not for heavy rigging of big pieces.

Before each job check the rope for cut strands, glazing, and stiff spots, and look at the ring and thimble for grooves, cracks, or deformation. Rig within the rated strength of every component, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions.

faq.q: Can I use it as a choker on the piece?
faq.a: Yes. Many crews choke the piece and attach the lowering line to the sling. Keep loads within the sling's rating.

faq.q: What is the 14mm?
faq.a: It is the ring size given for this sling. Confirm the rated strength with the seller before rigging on it.

name: XTC 16 Steel Ring-to-Ring Friction Saver
title: XTC 16 Steel Ring-to-Ring Friction Saver
meta: A ring-to-ring friction saver built on XTC 16-strand rope with steel rings. Protects the tie-in and your climb line, and is retrievable from the ground. Tips inside.
tagline: A steel ring-to-ring friction saver on 16-strand rope for a protected tie-in.
summary: This ring-to-ring friction saver joins two steel rings with a length of XTC 16-strand rope. It protects the bark and your climbing line at the tie-in, and the two-ring design can be retrieved from the ground when you are done.
highlights: Two steel rings on XTC 16-strand rope
Steel rings stand up to rope wear
Protects bark and climb line at the tie-in
Can be set and retrieved from the ground
specs: Steel, one large and one small

p: In moving-rope climbing the line runs back and forth over the tie-in all day. Over bark that means heat, friction, and cambium damage, and a climb line full of grit. A friction saver gives the rope a smooth ring to run through instead, so climbing is easier and the tree is spared.

Steel rings resist grooving far better than aluminum where rope runs constantly. A ring-to-ring design can be pulled out from the ground by running the climb line through the small ring correctly. Compare other friction savers if you want a rope-only or adjustable model.

Install the saver over a sound union or limb of adequate size and make sure the rings sit where the climb line will run cleanly without crossing over itself. Load-test the system from the ground before you leave it.

Check the rope for cuts, glazing, and wear at the rings, and look at both rings for grooves before every climb. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Can I retrieve it from the ground?
faq.a: Yes, ring-to-ring savers are designed to be retrieved when rigged correctly. Learn the method from a trained climber before relying on it.

faq.q: Does it work for SRS?
faq.a: It is designed mainly for moving-rope climbing. For stationary rope, use an anchor setup that suits SRS.

name: Yale Phantom Adjustable Friction Saver
title: Yale Phantom Adjustable Friction Saver
meta: The Yale Phantom adjustable friction saver fits a wide range of stem sizes and protects your tie-in point. How the adjustment works, setup notes, and inspection.
tagline: An adjustable friction saver that fits small and large tie-in stems.
summary: The Yale Phantom adjustable friction saver lets you size the saver to the stem at your tie-in instead of carrying several fixed lengths. It protects the bark and your climb line while giving the rope a smooth path through the rings.
highlights: Adjustable length fits a wide range of stems
One saver instead of several fixed lengths

p: Fixed friction savers are simple, but the length that works on one tree is too short or too long on the next. An adjustable saver lets you snug it down on a small union or open it up for a big stem, so the rings sit where they should and the saver does not flop around.
When the rope section wears out, you can replace just the lanyard and keep the hardware. Browse our full line of friction savers to compare designs.

Install it as the instructions show, set the length so the rings sit cleanly, and weight the system from the ground before climbing. Adjustable savers usually take a little more setup than a fixed ring-to-ring, and some are not designed for retrieval from the ground, so plan your exit.

Before every climb inspect the rope for cuts, glazing, and stiff spots, and check the rings and adjuster for grooves and secure grip. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Can I replace the rope section?
faq.a: Yes. A replacement Phantom friction saver lanyard is available, so the hardware can be reused if it passes inspection.

faq.q: Can it be retrieved from the ground?
faq.a: Check the manufacturer's instructions. Adjustable savers often need the climber to install and remove them in the tree.

name: Gap Arborist Supply Double Locking Snap Hook
title: Double Locking Snap Hook for Arborist Lanyards
meta: A double locking snap hook for flipline and lanyard ends, chosen for gloved use on a tree job. How it is used, what to check on the markings, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A double locking snap for lanyard ends and flipline connections.
summary: A double locking snap hook is the classic connector on the end of a flipline or lanyard. The keeper must be pushed open in two separate motions, which helps stop the gate from rolling open against a D-ring or limb.

p: Snaps have been the go-to connector on fliplines for generations because they are quick to clip one-handed with gloves on. You will see them on lanyard ends, on rope-and-snap climbing setups, and on positioning lanyards in bucket trucks.
The double locking keeper needs two motions to open, so the gate cannot easily be pushed open by a D-ring or a branch. Compare other snap hooks if you need a specific gate size or material.
Clip only to compatible D-rings and connectors so the snap cannot roll and load against its keeper. Do not clip a snap around a limb or back onto its own line unless it is designed for that.

Before each use, check that the keeper springs closed and locks on its own, and look for cracks, wear, corrosion, and bent parts. Retire it if it fails any check. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Can I use this on my climbing line?
faq.a: Only if the snap's ratings and markings meet the requirements for life support in your system. Check the markings before use.

faq.q: What does double locking mean?
faq.a: The keeper needs two separate actions to open, which makes accidental opening much less likely.

name: Teufelberger Hi-Vee Split Tail
title: Teufelberger Hi-Vee Split Tail Hitch Cord
meta: The Teufelberger Hi-Vee split tail, a hitch cord for friction hitches in moving rope climbing. How a split tail works, matching it to your rope, and inspection.
tagline: A heat-resistant split tail for tying friction hitches on your climbing line.
summary: The Teufelberger Hi-Vee split tail is a length of hitch cord made for tying friction hitches on a climbing line. Climbers use it in moving-rope systems to grip the line, release smoothly, and hold under load.
highlights: Hitch cord sold as a split tail
Made for friction hitches on arborist lines
Pairs with a hitch-tending micro pulley

body.h: How a split tail fits your system
p: In a moving-rope system the friction hitch is what holds you and lets you descend. A split tail is a separate length of cord that ties the hitch onto your climb line, so you can replace the wear-heavy hitch without cutting the end off your rope. Most climbers tie a Distel, VT, or similar hitch and tend it with a micro pulley.
The hitch cord has to suit your climbing line's diameter and cover. Too loose and the hitch slips; too grabby and it locks up. See our other hitch cords and split tails to compare.

Hitch cord wears faster than anything else in your system because it takes the heat of every descent. Check it before every climb for glazing, flat or stiff spots, cover damage, and a hitch that no longer grabs evenly, and replace it early.

Tie and dress your hitch carefully and test it on the ground before leaving it. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Which climbing rope works with the Hi-Vee?
faq.a: Check Teufelberger's guidance for compatible rope diameters and test the hitch on your own line before climbing.

faq.q: How long does a split tail last?
faq.a: It depends on how much you descend on it. Replace it when you see glazing, stiffness, or cover wear.

name: Replacement Friction Pins for Chicane
title: Replacement Friction Pins for the Chicane
meta: Replacement friction pins for the Chicane SRS braking device. When to swap worn pins, how to check for wear, and why to follow the maker's service instructions.
tagline: Fresh friction pins to keep a Chicane braking smoothly on a stationary rope.
summary: These replacement friction pins for the Chicane let you renew the wear surfaces that the rope runs across. Worn pins change how the device brakes, so swapping them restores smooth, predictable friction on a stationary rope.

p: Every foot of rope you descend drags across the friction surfaces of an SRS device. Grit in the rope speeds that up, and over time the pins develop grooves or flat spots. Worn pins change the friction you get, which can make the descent grabby in one spot and slippery in another.
Replacing the pins is cheaper than replacing the whole device, as long as the rest of it passes inspection. Browse other SRS climbing devices if your device is due for retirement.

Install the pins exactly as the manufacturer's instructions show, and only if the maker permits user replacement. Check every fastener afterward and test the device on the ground, with your full weight and a backup, before you climb on it.

Inspect pins and frame before each climb for grooves, sharp edges, and cracks. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: How do I know the pins are worn?
faq.a: Look for grooves, flat spots, or sharp edges where the rope runs, and notice any change in how the device brakes.

faq.q: Can I fit these myself?
faq.a: Only if the manufacturer's instructions allow user replacement. If they do not, have the device serviced or retired.

name: Teufelberger KMtree Static Climbing Rope (Purple/Green)
title: Teufelberger KMtree Static Climbing Rope, Purple/Green
meta: Teufelberger KMtree in purple and green, a static kernmantle climbing rope for SRS and MRS tree work. How it handles, what to pair it with, and how to inspect it.
tagline: A static kernmantle climbing rope for arborists who climb SRS and MRS.
summary: Teufelberger KMtree is a static kernmantle climbing rope for tree work, here in a purple and green colorway. Low stretch makes it efficient for stationary-rope ascents and gives mechanical devices a consistent rope to work on.
highlights: Low stretch for efficient SRS ascents
Works with mechanical devices and hitches
Purple/green color is easy to spot

body.h: Where a static kernmantle rope shines
p: In a stationary rope system, stretch is wasted effort: every bounce at the start of an ascent is energy you do not get back. A static kernmantle line keeps that to a minimum, so footlocking, rope walking, and ascending with a chest ascender feel direct. It also gives SRS devices a consistent diameter and firm cover to grip.
The same rope works for moving-rope climbing with a compatible hitch. See our other static climbing ropes if you want to compare handling and diameter.
Check that your devices, hitch cord, and ascenders are rated for this rope's diameter before you climb on it. Static rope can feel stiff at first; it usually softens with use.

Before every climb run the whole rope through your hands, feeling for cuts, glazing, soft or flat spots, and cover damage. Keep it away from saws, chemicals, and fuel, and store it in a rope bag out of sunlight. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Can I use KMtree for moving-rope climbing?
faq.a: Yes, with a compatible hitch and hitch cord. Test the hitch on the ground before leaving it.

faq.q: What length should I buy?
faq.a: Most climbers choose 150 ft for general work and 200 ft for big trees. Check available lengths in the listing.

name: Yale Phantom Green and Purple 11mm Climbing Rope
title: Yale Phantom 11mm Climbing Rope, Green and Purple
h1: Yale Phantom Green and Purple 11mm Climbing Rope
meta: Yale Phantom 11mm climbing rope in green and purple, a static climbing line for SRS and moving rope work. How it handles, device fit, and inspection tips.
tagline: An 11mm static climbing line for arborists running SRS devices or hitches.
summary: Yale Phantom is an 11mm climbing rope for arborists, shown here in green and purple. Its low-stretch construction suits stationary-rope ascents and gives mechanical devices a consistent line to work on.
highlights: Works with SRS devices and friction hitches
Green/purple color is easy to spot

p: An 11mm line is a popular size for stationary rope systems: light enough to haul and stuff in a bag, but with enough body for hitches and mechanical devices to grip. Low stretch means less bounce when you start an ascent and a more direct feel when rope walking.
Matching Phantom lanyards and friction saver rope are also available if you like a consistent setup. Compare other static climbing ropes if you want a different diameter.
Confirm that every device, ascender, and hitch cord in your system is rated for 11mm rope before you climb on it. Some devices work at the edge of their range on thinner lines, so test on the ground.

Inspect the full length before every climb for cuts, glazing, soft or flat spots, and cover damage. Keep it out of the sun and away from fuel and bar oil, and store it in a rope bag. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: Is 11mm too thin for my devices?
faq.a: Many arborist devices accept 11mm, but check each device's rated range before climbing on it.

faq.q: Can I climb MRS on Phantom?
faq.a: Yes, with a compatible hitch and hitch cord. Test the hitch on the ground before climbing.

name: Notch Tri-Guard II Stump Grinder Guard
title: Notch Tri-Guard II Stump Grinder Guard
h1: Notch Tri-Guard II Stump Grinder Guard
meta: The Notch Tri-Guard II stump grinder guard sets up around the work to catch flying chips and rocks. Why crews carry one, how to set it, and its limits on the job.
tagline: A portable debris guard that catches chips and rocks thrown by a stump grinder.
summary: The Notch Tri-Guard II is a portable stump grinder guard that stands between the cutter wheel and whatever you need to protect. It catches chips, dirt, and stones before they hit windows, cars, siding, or people.
highlights: Portable debris shield for stump grinding
Sets up quickly beside the stump

p: A stump grinder throws material hard and far, and one rock through a sliding door wipes out the profit on the job. A portable guard set between the wheel and the house, car, or street catches most of that debris and keeps it close to the stump, which also makes cleanup faster.
It is especially useful on tight residential lots, along sidewalks, and next to parked cars. See the rest of our stump grinding gear for teeth and accessories.

Place the guard on the side where debris would do the most damage, close enough to catch the throw but clear of the cutter wheel and the machine's swing. Reposition it as you work around the stump, and pick rocks and metal out of the work area before you start.
A guard reduces flying debris but does not replace a safe exclusion zone. Keep bystanders well back, wear eye, face, and hearing protection, and follow the grinder maker's manual and ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Does the guard replace a drop zone or exclusion area?
faq.a: No. It reduces flying debris, but you still need to keep people a safe distance from the grinder.

faq.q: Does it work with any stump grinder?
faq.a: It is a free-standing guard, so it can be used beside most grinders. Keep it clear of the cutter wheel.

name: Sterling TriTech 11mm Rope by the Foot
title: Sterling TriTech 11mm Rope by the Foot
h1: Sterling TriTech 11mm Rope by the Foot
meta: Sterling TriTech 11mm rope sold by the foot for building custom lanyards and fliplines. What it is used for, how to spec a length, and splicing and inspection notes.
tagline: 11mm Sterling TriTech cut to length for custom lanyards and fliplines.
summary: Sterling TriTech 11mm rope is sold by the foot so you can build a custom lanyard, flipline, or positioning component at the exact length you want. It is the same rope Sterling uses in its TriTech lanyards.
highlights: Same rope as Sterling TriTech lanyards

body.h: Why buy rope by the foot
p: Off-the-shelf lanyards come in a few lengths. If you climb big spars, work in a bucket, or just like a specific length, buying rope by the foot lets you build exactly what you need and re-use your existing snap and adjuster.

Measure your current lanyard, then add enough for terminations: a sewn eye, a spliced eye, or a stopper knot all take rope. Browse our tech cordage section for hitch cord and other cut-to-length rope.

Any eye or termination used for life support must be made by a qualified person using a method the rope maker approves, or tied with a knot you have been trained on. A home-made splice in rope you are not familiar with is not a shortcut worth taking.

Inspect the rope before each climb for cuts, glazing, and stiff or flat spots, and keep the saw well clear of any rope lanyard. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: How much should I order for a lanyard?
faq.a: Measure the working length you want and add enough for your terminations. When in doubt, order a little extra.

faq.q: Can I splice TriTech myself?
faq.a: Only if you are trained in a splice the manufacturer approves for this rope. Otherwise have it spliced by a qualified splicer.

name: Courant Sushi 1.8mm Throwline
title: Courant Sushi 1.8mm Throwline
meta: Courant Sushi 1.8mm throwline for setting climbing and rigging lines. How the slick line handles in a cube, isolating limbs, and caring for your throw line.
tagline: A slick 1.8mm throwline for setting lines high in the canopy.
summary: Courant Sushi is a 1.8mm throwline made for setting climbing and rigging lines. Its slick surface runs fast off a cube or bag and slides easily over bark when you isolate a limb.
highlights: Slides easily over bark when isolating
Bright color is easy to track

p: A good throwline has to come off the pile cleanly, fly far behind the bag, and then slide over bark without hanging up while you isolate the limb. A slick, thin line like the Sushi does all three, so you get more height with less arm.

1.8mm is a common middle ground: thin enough to throw high, thick enough to handle and pull a climbing line without cutting your hands. Compare other throw lines if you prefer a thinner or stiffer line.
Store it in a cube or bag so it pays out without tangles, and keep it clean; sap and grit slow it down. Check the line for nicks and thin spots, and cut out damage rather than throwing on it.
Throw lines are not life-support gear. Use them only to set your climbing or rigging line, and make sure the crew is clear of the drop zone when you throw or pull a bag down.

faq.q: Can I use a 1.8mm throwline with any throw weight?
faq.a: Yes, it works with standard throw bags. Lighter bags fly further on thin line; heavier bags pull it through dense crowns.

faq.q: How do I store it?
faq.a: Flake it into a throw cube or bag so it comes out without knots.

name: FTC 1.6mm Stiffline Yellow 80m
title: FTC 1.6mm Stiffline Throw Line, Yellow, 80m
meta: FTC Stiffline in 1.6mm yellow, an 80m throw line with a stiff, tangle-resistant body for setting climbing lines. How it handles, storage, and when to choose it.
tagline: An 80m, 1.6mm stiff throw line in bright yellow for long, high throws.
summary: FTC Stiffline is a 1.6mm throw line in yellow, supplied in an 80m length. Its stiffer body resists tangling and pays out cleanly, while the thin diameter helps a throw bag reach high crotches.
highlights: Bright yellow is easy to see in the canopy

p: Soft throw line flies well but can knot on itself in the cube or wrap around twigs in the canopy. A stiffer line holds its shape, comes off the pile with fewer snarls, and is easier to work back through branches when you are isolating a union.
At 1.6mm it is thin enough for long throws, and 80m is plenty for tall trees with line to spare. Compare other throw lines if you prefer a softer or thicker line.
Flake it into a throw cube or bag and let it pay out freely. Thin line can be hard on bare hands when pulling a heavy climbing line up, so wear gloves or use a thicker line for big hauls.
Check for nicks and thin spots and cut out damage. Throw line is not life-support gear; use it only to set your climbing or rigging line, and keep the crew out of the drop zone when throwing.

faq.q: Is 80m enough?
faq.a: For most trees, yes. It gives you enough line to go up and over a high limb and back to the ground with extra.

faq.q: Stiff or soft throw line?
faq.a: Stiff line tangles less and pushes through branches better; soft line often flies a bit further. Many climbers carry both.

name: Notch Acculine 2.2mm Throw Line
title: Notch Acculine 2.2mm Throw Line
meta: Notch Acculine 2.2mm throw line, a heavier throw line that is easy on the hands and good for pulling up climb lines. How it handles, when to choose it, and care.
tagline: A 2.2mm throw line that is easy to grip and strong enough for hauling lines.
summary: Notch Acculine 2.2mm throw line is a slightly heavier throw line that is easy to grip and pull. It suits climbers who want a line that handles well with gloves and hauls a climbing line up without cutting into the hands.
highlights: Good for hauling up climbing lines

body.h: When a thicker throw line makes sense
p: Thin throw line flies further, but it can be hard to hold and harsh on the hands when you haul a long climbing line up through the crown. At 2.2mm, Acculine gives you more to grab, tangles less, and is easier to manage with gloves on. You give up a little height on the throw for that comfort.
It is a good choice for lower crotches, frequent line setting, and crews who use the throw line to pull up rigging lines. Compare other throw lines for thinner options.
Store it flaked in a cube or bag, keep it clean of sap and grit, and cut out nicked or worn sections. Pair it with a throw weight heavy enough to pull the thicker line through the canopy.
Throw line is not life-support gear. Use it only to set your climbing or rigging line, and keep everyone clear of the drop zone when throwing and when pulling a bag down.

faq.q: Will 2.2mm throw as high as thinner line?
faq.a: Usually not quite as high, because thicker line adds drag. It makes up for that with easier handling.

faq.q: What weight bag should I use?
faq.a: A slightly heavier bag helps pull thicker line through. Many climbers carry a few weights for different trees.

name: Weaver Denali Climbing Harness
title: Weaver Denali Climbing Harness for Tree Work
meta: The Weaver Denali climbing harness, a tree climbing saddle for arborists who want a supportive, practical harness. Fit, setup, and inspection notes before you buy.
tagline: A Weaver tree-climbing harness for daily climbing and work positioning.
summary: The Weaver Denali climbing harness is a tree climbing saddle for arborists who climb and position all day. Weaver has built saddles for tree workers for decades, and the Denali is a practical choice for climbers who want support and simple setup.
highlights: Attachment points for climbing and positioning

body.h: Choosing a harness for daily climbing
p: Your saddle is the one piece of gear you are attached to all day, so fit and comfort decide how you feel at quitting time. Look at how the waist and leg loops carry your weight when you sit back, how the attachment points line up with your climbing and positioning systems, and whether there is room to hang a saw, handsaw, and a few carabiners.
Compare the Denali with our other saddles and harnesses to find the right fit for your climbing style, whether that is mostly spurring removals or long pruning climbs.
Use the maker's sizing chart and adjust the harness so the waist sits snug above the hips and the legs do not pinch when you sit. Hang in it on the ground before climbing.

Check the label to confirm the harness is certified for the work you do. Inspect the webbing, stitching, buckles, and attachment points before every climb, and retire it if you find cuts, burns, or worn stitching. Treat it as life-support equipment: it must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected before every climb, and be used only by trained climbers.

faq.q: How do I size the Denali?
faq.a: Use Weaver's sizing chart for waist and leg measurements, then adjust and test it hanging on the ground.

faq.q: Can I use it for SRS?
faq.a: Check the manufacturer's instructions for approved attachment points and configurations before setting up an SRS system.

name: Hardhead Jr Wedge
title: Hardhead Jr Felling Wedge
meta: The Hardhead Jr wedge, a compact felling and bucking wedge that keeps the kerf open and the bar free. When to use a small wedge, setting it, and when to replace it.
tagline: A compact plastic wedge for bucking and felling smaller trees.
summary: The Hardhead Jr wedge is a compact felling and bucking wedge for smaller wood. Tap it into the back cut or a bucking kerf to keep the saw from pinching and to help steer the tree toward the notch.
highlights: Compact size for smaller trees and logs
Keeps the kerf open so the bar does not pinch
Safe to hit with the chain nearby
Fits in a pocket or wedge pouch

body.h: Where a small wedge earns its keep
p: Not every cut needs a big felling wedge. On small trees, limbs on the ground, and bucking cuts, a compact wedge slips into a narrow kerf quickly and stops the bar from getting pinched. It is light enough to carry several on a belt or in a pocket.
For bigger trees and heavy back-leaners, step up to a larger wedge. See our full range of felling wedges to build a set.

Set the wedge as soon as the back cut is deep enough, before the kerf starts to close. Drive it with an axe or wedge hammer, not with the saw. A plastic wedge is used because a chain that touches it is not ruined the way it would be on steel.

Retire a wedge that is cracked, badly mushroomed, or chewed up by the chain, because it can spit out of the cut. Felling should only be done by trained workers following ANSI Z133 and with a clear escape route.

faq.q: Is the Jr big enough for felling?
faq.a: It suits small trees and bucking. Use a larger wedge on bigger trees or when you need more lift.

faq.q: Can I hit it with a steel hammer?
faq.a: Yes, an axe poll or wedge hammer is normal. Replace the wedge once the head mushrooms badly.

name: Heavy Duty Multi-Tool Holster
title: Heavy Duty Multi-Tool Holster for Wedges and Tools
meta: A heavy duty multi-tool holster that hangs from a belt to carry wedges, a scrench, and small tools while you fell and buck. What fits, how to wear it, and care.
tagline: A belt holster that keeps wedges and small tools within reach on the ground.
summary: A heavy duty multi-tool holster rides on your belt and keeps wedges, a scrench, a file, and other small tools within reach while you fell and buck. No more walking back to the truck for a wedge in the middle of a cut.
highlights: Carries wedges and small tools on the belt
Keeps tools off the ground and out of the brush
Works with a logging or tool belt

p: When the back cut starts to close, you need a wedge right now, not one sitting on the tailgate. A belt holster keeps two or three wedges, a scrench, and a file on your hip so they are always there when the saw stops, and they do not get lost in brush and sawdust.
Pair it with a logging belt and a set of plastic wedges for a complete felling kit. See our other wedges and holsters for wedges to fill it.
Wear the holster on your non-saw side so it does not catch on the saw or your chaps, and carry only what you need so it does not drag on your belt. Keep sharp tools sheathed.

Shake sawdust out at the end of the day and let it dry out if it gets wet. Felling and bucking should only be done by trained workers wearing chaps, helmet, eye and hearing protection, following ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will it fit on any belt?
faq.a: It is made to hang from a work or logging belt. Check the belt loop size against your belt.

faq.q: How many wedges does it hold?
faq.a: That depends on wedge size. Most sawyers carry two or three wedges plus a scrench.

name: Husqvarna File Handle for Chainsaw File
title: Husqvarna File Handle for Chainsaw Files
h1: Husqvarna File Handle for Chain Saw File
meta: A Husqvarna file handle for round chainsaw files. Gives a solid grip, steadier strokes, and a safer sharpening job on the tailgate. Fit, use, and care tips here.
tagline: A simple grip for round chainsaw files, for steadier and safer sharpening.
summary: A Husqvarna file handle fits on the tang of a round chainsaw file and gives you a full grip while sharpening. It makes your strokes steadier and keeps the bare tang out of your palm.
highlights: Keeps the tang out of your hand
Cheap and easy to keep in the kit

p: Filing a chain with a bare file is uncomfortable and inconsistent. A handle gives you leverage and control, so you can hold the angle and push every cutter the same number of strokes, which is how you get a chain that cuts straight.
It also keeps the pointed tang out of your palm. Keep one on each size of file in your kit. Find files and guides in our wrenches and files section.

File on the push stroke only, lifting off on the return, and match the file size to your chain pitch. Count strokes per cutter so both sides stay even, and check the depth gauges every few sharpenings.
Set the chain brake or shut the saw off, wear gloves, and clamp the bar in a vise or stump vise. Replace the file once it stops biting cleanly.

faq.q: Does it fit all round files?
faq.a: It is made for round chainsaw files. Check that the file tang seats firmly in the handle.

faq.q: Why does my chain cut crooked after filing?
faq.a: Usually uneven filing between sides. A handle and a consistent stroke count help.

name: Replacement File for Guide Bar Dresser
title: Replacement File for Guide Bar Dresser
h1: Replacement File for Guide Bar Dresser
meta: A replacement flat file for a guide bar dresser. Swap a dull file and keep dressing chainsaw bar rails square and burr-free. Fit notes and bar care tips inside.
tagline: A fresh flat file for your guide bar dresser.
summary: This replacement file for a guide bar dresser restores the cutting edge on the tool you use to square up chainsaw bar rails. A sharp file cuts burrs off cleanly instead of skating over them.
highlights: Replacement flat file for a bar dresser

p: Bar dresser files dull just like chain files. When the file skates over the rail instead of biting, or it takes many strokes to remove a burr, it is time for a new one. A dull file can also round over the rail edges you are trying to square.
Check that the file matches your dresser before ordering. Browse our wrenches and files section for bar dressers and other sharpening tools.

Dress the rails at each chain change, flip the bar so it wears evenly, and clean the groove and oil holes. Replace the bar when the rails are badly worn or the groove is too shallow to hold the chain upright.
Wear gloves when handling the bar and chain, and keep the file clean with a file card so it keeps cutting.

faq.q: Will this fit my bar dresser?
faq.a: Check the file size against your dresser. It is meant as a replacement for a guide bar dresser file.

faq.q: How do I keep the file cutting?
faq.a: Clean it with a file card and keep it dry to prevent rust.

name: Timber Savage Soft Grip File Handle
title: Timber Savage Soft Grip Chainsaw File Handle
h1: Timber Savage Soft Grip File Handle
meta: The Timber Savage soft grip file handle for round chainsaw files. A comfortable, secure grip for steady, even sharpening in the field. Fit and use tips inside.
tagline: A cushioned handle for round chainsaw files and comfortable field sharpening.
summary: The Timber Savage soft grip file handle fits round chainsaw files and gives you a cushioned, non-slip grip. It helps you hold the angle and keep strokes even, especially with cold or gloved hands.

p: Field sharpening is usually done on a tailgate or a stump, often with cold hands. A soft, grippy handle is easier to hold steady than a hard plastic one, so the file stays at the right angle and each cutter gets the same strokes.
Keep a handle on each file size you carry. You can find files, guides, and bar tools in our wrenches and files section.
Match the file to your chain pitch, file on the push stroke only, and count strokes per cutter. Check depth gauges every few sharpenings and keep both sides even.
Shut off the saw or set the chain brake, wear gloves, and support the bar firmly while filing. Replace the file when it stops biting.

faq.q: Does it fit all round files?
faq.a: It is made for round chainsaw files. Check that the tang seats firmly.

faq.q: Is a soft grip better than a standard handle?
faq.a: It is mainly about comfort and grip, especially with cold or gloved hands.
